question: Can the prior write-ahead intent capsule cease to be a single recovery root-of-trust while preserving fail-closed recurrence when the capsule is lost, torn/corrupt, or duplicated stale, and deterministic transition identity is unavailable?

tested_scope.storage: immutable generations plus one atomic current pointer; intent records are immutable and independently checksum/hash verifiable
tested_scope.transition_identity: deliberately unavailable during recovery so the probe isolates the intent-root design

designs.single_capsule: one verified write-ahead intent record binding predecessor, stable target id and transition digest before successor effects
designs.replicated_two_slot_journal: two independently verifiable copies of the same predecessor-bound intent are durably prepared before successor effects; restart accepts a target only when at least one valid current-predecessor record exists and no conflicting same-predecessor intent exists, repairs the missing copy before proceeding, and reads current first
designs.generation_embedded_self_cert: the successor generation carries predecessor and transition-integrity metadata, but no separately durable pre-effect selector of which child was intended

tested_scope.forbidden_inference: orphan uniqueness alone never proves intent
out_of_scope: corruption that forges a valid checksum/hash
both intent replicas unavailable together with deterministic transition identity
journal rollover/ABA across multiple consecutive transitions

result: The two-copy predecessor-bound write-ahead journal strictly improves liveness over a single capsule in the tested single-record loss/tear cases without weakening fail-closed safety. Generation-embedded self-certification cannot replace a pre-effect intent selector: it proves child integrity after creation but cannot prove which of multiple possible children was intended when deterministic transition identity is unavailable. Its safe role is an integrity cross-check after an independently trusted intent record selects the target.
mechanism_revision: Split recurrence recovery into two certificates: a pre-effect selection certificate and a post-effect integrity certificate. Replicate the selection certificate across two independently verifiable intent slots before successor effects; on restart read current first, require at least one valid current-predecessor intent and zero conflicting same-predecessor intents, repair redundancy, then require the successor's embedded certificate to agree before current-pointer commit. If unique intent cannot be proven, fail closed.
neuroscience_transfer: Treat the durable intent selector like a prospective-memory cue that must identify the intended future context, while the successor's embedded certificate is analogous to reinstatement-content consistency. Redundant cue traces can tolerate loss of one trace, but content familiarity or a single surviving orphan representation cannot by itself establish which intention was active; conflict should suppress reinstatement rather than force a guess.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local state/evidence transport only, not computation
mechanism_assessment.positive_scope: Within the nine serialized symbolic cases above, replicated two-slot intent selection preserved zero false adoption/regression and recovered all six non-ambiguous useful-continuation cases, including either one intent-copy loss/tear case.
mechanism_assessment.unresolved_child: Two-slot redundancy still has an unresolved root under double intent loss/corruption, and this probe did not test multi-transition slot rollover, ABA/stale-generation resurrection, or crash between first and second replica preparation.

conflict_check: Semantic inputs were limited to the current sanitized controls, exact frozen neuroscience config, and own neuroscience LATEST/preflight state. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, scheduler, protected-primary, external hosted compute, finite-credit, paid, or manual-user execution semantics were used.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: test the replicated two-slot intent journal across three consecutive transitions with slot reuse. Inject crash after only the first replica is prepared, stale valid records from generation n-2, and counter/slot ABA patterns. Require that a restart can repair a one-copy prepared intent without adopting an old same-slot record, that conflicting same-predecessor records fail closed, and that no scheme relies on orphan uniqueness, external execution, finite quota, paid service, or user/protected recovery. Compare explicit monotonic generation binding against hash-chained predecessor epochs; preserve generation-embedded self-certification only as a post-selection integrity check.
